To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) 25% of news shared on Twitter in 2016 was fake news, 2) fake news was spread by a relatively small group of users, and 3) fake news spreaders were more likely to be influenced by Trump supporters than Clinton supporters.

We find that, while traditional center and left-leaning news outlets largely influence the activity and behavior of Clinton supporters, we see a reverse causality for fake news: the dynamics of the activity of Trump's supporters influence the spread of fake news."

(a) fake news was spread by a relatively small number of accounts that were highly active; (b) these fake news accounts were followed by a relatively small group of users who were very active; (c) the activity of Trump's followers influenced the activity of the fake news spreaders; and (d) the activity of the Clinton's followers influenced the spread of traditional media news.
